outputs.L3:
The invention relates to a drug packaging device equipped with an inkjet printing unit capable of printing information on packaging paper with high quality, without requiring a support member, platen, or other base directly behind the packaging paper during printing.

The drug packaging device includes a drug supply unit, a packaging unit, a packaging paper conveying unit, and a printing unit. The drug supply unit supplies drugs to be packaged, and the packaging unit packages the supplied drugs using packaging paper. The packaging paper conveying unit conveys the packaging paper along a predetermined conveyance path toward the packaging unit. The printing unit is arranged along this conveyance path and prints information, such as patient names, dosage instructions, drug identification information, dates, or other necessary data, on the packaging paper before or during the packaging process.

The printing unit includes an ink ejection unit configured to eject ink in a downward direction. The ink ejection unit may be an inkjet head that ejects ink droplets toward the packaging paper in accordance with printing data. Because the ink is ejected downward, the influence of gravity on the ink droplets is stabilized, thereby contributing to accurate droplet landing positions and improved print quality.

The conveyance path of the packaging paper includes a section in which the packaging paper is conveyed in a direction that intersects the direction in which the ink is ejected. In this intersecting-direction conveyance section, the packaging paper passes below the ink ejection unit while being held in a stretched state by the structure of the conveyance path. As a result, the ink ejection unit can print on the packaging paper even though no support or base is arranged immediately behind the printing surface of the paper.

More specifically, the packaging paper conveyance path includes an upstream direction-switching section and a downstream direction-switching section. These direction-switching sections change the traveling direction of the packaging paper and define the intersecting-direction conveyance section between them. The ink ejection unit is positioned at a predetermined distance above this intersecting-direction conveyance section. By arranging the ink ejection unit in this manner, a suitable gap is maintained between the ink ejection unit and the packaging paper, enabling stable ink ejection and high-quality printing.

With this configuration, the packaging paper can be conveyed reliably while maintaining an appropriate posture for printing. Since printing can be performed without placing a support member behind the packaging paper, the device can avoid problems such as ink adhering to a support surface, contamination of the packaging paper, smearing of printed information, and increased maintenance requirements. Accordingly, the invention provides a compact and efficient drug packaging device capable of performing high-quality inkjet printing on packaging paper.
outputs.L4:
A drug packaging device is proposed in which information can be printed directly onto packaging paper by means of an inkjet printing unit that ejects ink downward. The packaging paper is conveyed along a transport path that includes a section extending in a direction intersecting the ink ejection direction, as well as direction-switching sections that guide the paper before and after printing. Instead of supporting the packaging paper from below with a base or platen at the printing position, the paper is held and transported by the configuration of the conveyance path itself.

With this arrangement, the inkjet printing unit can print required information, such as patient names, drug names, dosage instructions, dates, barcodes, or other identification data, onto the packaging paper while the paper is being conveyed through the device. Because the printing unit ejects ink downward, stable ink discharge and accurate landing of ink droplets can be achieved. At the same time, the intersecting-direction conveyance path and the direction-switching sections allow the packaging paper to pass through the printing region in a controlled manner without the need for a separate support structure directly beneath the printing area.

This eliminates or reduces the need for a base member that would otherwise support the packaging paper during printing. As a result, the overall structure of the drug packaging device can be simplified, the number of components can be reduced, and maintenance and cleaning can be made easier. In addition, by avoiding contact with a support base at the printing position, the device can reduce the risk of ink smearing, paper contamination, or mechanical interference during conveyance.

Accordingly, the proposed configuration enables high-quality printing on packaging paper while maintaining a compact and simplified device structure. The drug packaging device can therefore reliably prepare printed packaging paper for enclosing prescribed drugs, while achieving good print performance without requiring a dedicated support mechanism beneath the printing unit.

**The Power of “The”**

The word **“the”** is one of the most common words in the English language, yet it plays an important role in communication. It is a definite article, used to point to a specific person, place, thing, or idea. For example, when we say “the book,” we are talking about a particular book, not just any book.

Although it is a small word, **“the”** helps make sentences clearer and more precise. It gives meaning, direction, and focus to what we say. Without it, many sentences would sound incomplete or confusing.

In writing and speech, **“the”** often goes unnoticed, but it is essential. It connects ideas smoothly and helps readers and listeners understand exactly what is being discussed. Sometimes, the smallest words carry the greatest importance.

counterfactuals.output:
【要約】

【課題】  
薬剤包装機において、包装紙に対してインクを下向きに吐出して印刷を行う場合であっても、包装紙の印字面をプラテンや支持部材で受けることなく、印字位置の乱れ、インクのにじみ、着弾精度の低下等を抑制し、高品位な印刷を安定して行うことができる薬剤包装機を提供する。

【解決手段】  
薬剤を分包するための包装紙を搬送する包装紙搬送部と、前記包装紙に薬剤情報等を印刷するインクジェット印刷部とを備える薬剤包装機であって、前記インクジェット印刷部は、包装紙の搬送経路の上方に配置され、インクを下向きに吐出する印字ヘッドを有する。前記包装紙は、印字ヘッドに対向する印字領域において、プラテン又は印字面を直接支持する支持部材を介することなく搬送される。さらに、包装紙搬送部は、印字領域の上流側及び下流側で包装紙に所定の張力を付与し、印字領域における包装紙の姿勢及び高さ位置を安定化させる張力付与機構を備える。また、印字ヘッドと包装紙との間隔を所定範囲に維持するように、包装紙の搬送速度、張力、及び印字タイミングの少なくとも一つを制御する制御部を備える。

【効果】  
本発明によれば、印字領域にプラテンや支持部材を設けないため、包装紙の裏面側への接触による汚染、摩擦、紙粉の発生、インクの転写等を抑制できる。また、包装紙を適切な張力状態で搬送することにより、印字ヘッドから下向きに吐出されたインクの着弾位置を安定させることができ、文字、バーコード、患者名、服薬時期、薬剤情報等を鮮明に印刷できる。これにより、薬剤包装機の衛生性及び保守性を向上させつつ、プラテンレス構成で高い印字品質を実現することができる。

counterfactuals.prompt: Compose a patent-style “object and configuration” description for an inkjet-equipped drug packaging machine that can print on packaging paper with high quality without using a support, base, or similar backing member.
counterfactuals.output:
**Object**

An object of the present invention is to provide a drug packaging machine equipped with an inkjet printing unit, the machine being capable of performing high-quality printing on packaging paper while the packaging paper is conveyed, without requiring a support member, backing plate, platen, base, or similar backing member disposed opposite an inkjet head.  

Another object is to prevent deterioration in print quality caused by fluttering, waviness, displacement, or deformation of the packaging paper in a printing region, while maintaining a simple structure that is easy to clean and suitable for use in a drug packaging environment.  

A further object is to provide a drug packaging machine in which ink mist, paper dust, and deposited foreign matter are less likely to accumulate near the inkjet head, thereby reducing maintenance frequency and improving reliability of printed information such as patient names, drug names, administration timing, dosage instructions, barcodes, and identification codes.

**Configuration**

The drug packaging machine includes a packaging paper conveyance path along which packaging paper is conveyed, a drug supply unit configured to supply drugs to the packaging paper, a sealing unit configured to seal the packaging paper so as to form individual drug packages, and an inkjet printing unit configured to print predetermined information on the packaging paper before, during, or after formation of the drug packages.

The inkjet printing unit includes an inkjet head having a nozzle surface provided with a plurality of ink discharge nozzles. The inkjet head is arranged so that the nozzle surface faces one surface of the packaging paper in a printing region. In the printing region, no support member, backing plate, platen, base, roller, or other backing member is disposed on the opposite surface side of the packaging paper at a position facing the nozzle surface. The packaging paper is therefore printed in a non-backed state.

The packaging paper conveyance path is configured to maintain the packaging paper in a tensioned state at least in the printing region. More specifically, the packaging paper is guided by upstream and downstream guide members disposed respectively upstream and downstream of the printing region in a conveyance direction, and a tension applying mechanism applies a predetermined conveyance tension to the packaging paper between the upstream and downstream guide members. By this tension, the packaging paper is held substantially flat in the printing region without being supported from the rear side.

The inkjet head is disposed at a predetermined gap from the packaging paper. The predetermined gap is set to a range in which ink droplets discharged from the inkjet head land accurately on the packaging paper while avoiding contact between the nozzle surface and the packaging paper even when slight vibration or displacement of the packaging paper occurs. The gap may be adjusted by a head position adjusting mechanism configured to move the inkjet head toward and away from the packaging paper.

In one configuration, the printing region is formed between two conveyance rollers, guide rollers, or paper holding portions positioned on opposite sides of the printing region in the conveyance direction. These rollers or holding portions define the travel position of the packaging paper and suppress fluttering of the paper without contacting the paper at a location directly opposite the inkjet head. Thus, the packaging paper is stabilized only by tension and peripheral guidance, while an open space is maintained behind the packaging paper in the region facing the inkjet head.

The drug packaging machine may further include a suction or airflow control unit positioned near the printing region but not functioning as a backing member contacting or supporting the rear surface of the packaging paper. The suction or airflow control unit may generate a weak airflow for removing ink mist or paper dust from the vicinity of the nozzle surface or for suppressing turbulence around the printing region. The airflow is controlled so as not to deform the packaging paper to an extent that impairs printing accuracy.

The inkjet printing unit may be controlled in synchronization with conveyance of the packaging paper. A controller receives conveyance information from an encoder, sensor, or drive motor control signal and controls ink discharge timing of the inkjet head according to the position of the packaging paper. The controller may also control paper tension, conveyance speed, and head-to-paper gap so that printing is performed while the packaging paper is maintained in a stable non-backed state.

With this configuration, high-quality inkjet printing can be performed directly on packaging paper used for drug packaging without providing a platen, backing plate, support base, or similar member opposite the inkjet head. Accordingly, contamination and accumulation of ink or paper dust on a backing member can be avoided, the structure around the printing region can be simplified, cleaning performance can be improved, and clear printed information can be formed on each drug package.
